subject.title: [Feature]: models.providers.*.enabled flag to disable providers without removing config

question: Should OpenClaw add a public `models.providers.<id>.enabled?: boolean` contract, and what should happen when the disabled provider is the selected primary or an explicit fallback?
rationale: Source inspection proves the requested behavior is missing, but adding a public config surface and changing provider routing/fallback semantics requires maintainer intent under repository config-compatibility policy.

options.title: Approve shared provider eligibility
options.body: Add the flag and one shared eligibility helper used by schema, planning, fallback, catalog/list/status/probe paths, docs, and tests, including disabled-primary semantics.

options.title: Reject provider-level disable
options.body: Keep the current model where operators remove provider blocks or edit fallback lists to avoid adding another public config knob.

options.title: Defer provider lifecycle design
options.body: Hold this until provider enablement, plugin setup, auth/status, and model-picker lifecycle behavior are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve shared provider eligibility
recommendation.body: Add the flag and one shared eligibility helper used by schema, planning, fallback, catalog/list/status/probe paths, docs, and tests, including disabled-primary semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent model/provider identity, selection, and runtime refactor history makes this the best available owner for the shared config-routing decision.
